text: You scan a code and type a PIN. A second later, the shop has your money.
How does money cross two banks that fast? By the end, you will follow one payment from your phone to the shop.
N P C I, the National Payments Corporation of India, built UPI.
There is your app, a central switch run by N P C I, your bank, and the shop's bank.
You do not need the shop's account number. A UPI I D, like this one, stands in for it.
You pick the payee, enter the amount, and your PIN. The app sends the request to the switch.
The switch finds the shop's bank from the UPI I D, and asks yours.
Your bank checks the PIN and your balance, then takes the money out.
The shop's bank adds it, and a confirmation travels back to both of you.
A central switch links the two banks, so one request moves the money.
One switch joins two banks, so a single request debits you and credits the shop. In August 2025, UPI handled about twenty billion payments.
